reviews.body: Thank you for the contribution. I have a few minor suggestions to tidy this up, otherwise looks good.

review_comments.body:
**AIKIDO-2026-531524 in undici** - medium severity
When a client composed the cache interceptor with a downstream handler that threw during cached-response replay, the throw could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled rejection and terminate the Node.js process. A malicious or compromised HTTP server could trigger this by serving a cacheable response that exceeded `dump`’s configured `maxSize` or had more than five `Content-Encoding` values; stale-entry revalidation could also trigger it.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Remediation** Aikido suggests bumping this package to version 8.12.4 to resolve this issue

<sub>Reply `@AikidoSec ignore: [REASON]` to ignore this issue.</sub>
<sub>[More info](https://app.aikido.dev/repositories/1854557/pull_requests/1300/latest?groupId=85165)</sub>
</details>
@pcbeingused333 Can you please address this version bump? Thank you

comments.body:
Thank you for your contribution! We've added this to our internal tracking system for review.
ID: PM-47264
Link: https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-47264

Details on our contribution process can be found here: https://contributing.bitwarden.com/contributing/pull-requests/community-pr-process.

Thanks @BTreston. Done in the new commit: `getProxyUrl`, `getProxyAgent` and `getFetchOptions` now live in `NodeUtils` (`libs/utils/nodeUtils.ts`) and `EntraIdDirectoryService` calls them (`fetchOptions: NodeUtils.getFetchOptions()`, `agent: NodeUtils.getProxyAgent()`). `undici` is bumped to 8.12.4 in package.json (dependency + override) and the lockfile, per the Aikido note.

I did not change `NodeApiService.nativeFetch`: since #1289 it delegates to Electron's `net.fetch`, which uses Chromium's network stack (system proxy settings and the OS certificate store, which is what fixed the self-hosted CA case). Swapping it for global `fetch` with an `agent` property would drop that behaviour, since Node's `fetch` (undici) ignores `agent`, and it would break the existing spec that asserts the `net.fetch` delegation. If you still want it consolidated, could you say which behaviour you'd like (e.g. `fetch` with `dispatcher: EnvHttpProxyAgent`)?

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
